question: If \(p\ge5\) is a prime number, then \(24\) divides \(p^2-1\) without remainder
solution:
Factoring reveals two nearby integers whose divisibility is easy to track:
\[
p^2-1=(p-1)(p+1).
\]
A prime \(p\ge5\) is divisible by neither \(2\) nor \(3\). In particular, \(p\) is odd, so \(p-1\) and \(p+1\) are consecutive even integers. One is divisible by \(4\), and the other is divisible by \(2\). Their product is therefore divisible by \(8\).

Among the three consecutive integers \(p-1,p,p+1\), exactly one is divisible by \(3\). It cannot be \(p\), so one of the two factors \(p-1\) and \(p+1\) is divisible by \(3\). Their product is thus divisible by \(3\) as well as \(8\).

The least common multiple of \(3\) and \(8\) is \(24\), so \(24\) divides \(p^2-1\) for every allowed prime. The answer is \(\boxed{\text{always}}\), choice C.
